report:
Initial stage: Two focal accounts explicitly narrate Experiment acquisition, comprising five product acquisition categories: A04’s Super Saturated, Buffer Jelly, face wash and mesh moisturizer, plus A05’s Avant Guard checkout. These are account-level reports, not verified transactions or five established purchase events. No subsequent-stage evidence was supplied.

A04 describes expansion across the line after favorable experiences: a sister’s introduction preceded ordering Super Saturated; wanting stronger nighttime hydration/repair prompted Buffer Jelly; favorable subsequent experience preceded buying face wash and then the newly launched mesh moisturizer. Reported benefits include lightweight, fast-drying hydration before makeup, glowy skin after Buffer Jelly, and makeup removal, hydration and no more breakouts with the wash. These are sequential, same-person reports involving multiple products, not isolated efficacy tests. Colorful packaging also receives praise, without an explicit acquisition attribution. A05 explicitly links immediate Avant Guard checkout to TikTok discovery in the context of seeking sustainability after already stopping disposable sheet masks. Neither account establishes repurchase of the same product; A04’s refill metadata cannot supply that missing narration.

A01 reports putting Softwear back into an FF cart because of another commenter’s recommendation, not checkout or use. A02’s dislike of an intolerable-feeling product and consequent skipping concerns Dr. Idriss in parent context, alongside approval of its baste balm; it is not Experiment abandonment. A12’s cream 2.0 and cleanser acquisitions, post-tret moisturizer need, favorable formulation assessment and intention to try more concern Regimen Lab, not Experiment.

The two credited retailer-review origins independently repeat only the broad proposition of completed Experiment acquisition. Their specific products and reported reasons differ; no precise purchase motive is independently repeated or corroborated across source roles. A01 supplies a separate, explicitly self-attributed recommendation-to-cart consequence. No focal stock-up, gifted receipt, contemplated/completed return, or intended/completed routine substitution is narrated. A04’s claim that makeup remover is no longer needed is functional redundancy, not an explicit report of stopping it. A05’s prior sheet-mask discontinuation predates discovering Avant Guard.

Material context, excluded from focal counts: cowrunamuck (Reddit t1_nclxocd, 2025-09-05, score 21) reports two Softwear backups because of love for the product and previously difficult website-only acquisition, plus enthusiasm for Sephora availability. They report smooth, moisturized lips despite sensitivity to other facial exfoliants, favor Softwear over Eadem, and dislike Eadem’s scent/taste while acknowledging its moisturizing effect. RowanVC (t1_ncls0z6, same thread/date, score 42) independently praises Softwear and Experiment generally; their unspecified lip-balm stash does not establish Experiment stockpiling. Their Dr. Idriss account describes stickiness, required layering and soft lips with lanolin or another mask. These are distinct contextual actors in one discussion, not focal acquisition testimony. Their Softwear praise cannot corroborate the private buying reasons of focal accounts.

Observed engagement: A01 score 13, A02 score 4, A12 score 12; each is explicitly marked material_positive=false and not_interpreted. A04 and A05 each have 0 upvotes and 0 downvotes, observation time unavailable. Context scores 21 and 42 remain raw; exposure and engagement observation times are unavailable. Likes/scores establish neither additional experiences nor independence, prevalence or purchase effects.

Conflict posture: none observed for the bounded narrated acquisition/cart actions; broader experiences contain qualifications. A05’s strong satisfaction coexists with imperfect cheek/nose fit; A04’s thickness/oiliness concern was anticipatory and followed by praise. A02’s discomfort and A12’s small-cleanser complaint belong to other brands and coexist with positive sentiment there. Formula versions are unspecified except A12’s other-brand cream 2.0. Evidence supports individual reported actions and reasons, not market causation, representative demand or verified buying.

source_index.findings: boxybrown84; Reddit 1n9da6u, 2025-09-05; score 13, material_positive=false/not_interpreted, observation time unavailable. Explicitly re-added Experiment balm to FF cart because of a comment; parent identifies Softwear, version unknown. No completed checkout, acquisition, use or stock-up. Parent cowrunamuck’s favorable experience and two backups are separate contextual testimony, not A01’s. Independence posture unavailable; same thread as A02.

PamelaDamnela; Reddit 1n9da6u, 2025-09-05; score 4, material_positive=false/not_interpreted, observation time unavailable. Owns but always skips an intolerable-feeling item; parent context resolves this to the Dr. Idriss exfoliator, alongside love for its baste balm. SKU/version not fully specified. No Experiment acquisition or adverse-use testimony, return or explicit completed routine substitution. Parent RowanVC’s Experiment praise and layered Dr. Idriss experience remain separate testimony. Independence posture unavailable.

Junip customer 202931541; review 7540631, published 2025-03-22, updated 2025-03-23; credited origin; 0 up/0 down, observation time unavailable. Four explicit Experiment acquisition categories: Super Saturated after sister introduction and liking it; Buffer Jelly for greater nighttime hydration/repair; face wash after favorable preceding experience; mesh moisturizer immediately upon launch. Wash and moisturizer correspond contextually to Plasma Wash and Molecular Mesh, but body does not give those exact names; versions unknown. Reports pre-makeup lightweight, refreshing, fast-drying hydration without clogged-feeling pores; glowy/clean skin after Jelly despite initial thick/oily concern; makeup removal, hydration and no more breakouts with wash. Multiple-product routine prevents isolated attribution. Loves packaging colors, without explicit buying causation. No same-product repurchase or stock-up established; makeup-remover redundancy is not narrated discontinuation. Metadata separately identifies Super Saturated Refill, verified buyer, unrewarded and Combo + Sensitive skin; refill metadata adds no acquisition category.

Junip customer 44968672; review 1569510, 2022-11-03, updated same date; credited origin; 0 up/0 down, observation time unavailable. Explicit immediate checkout of reusable Avant Guard after TikTok-creator discovery amid sustainability concerns. Had already stopped formerly near-nightly disposable sheet masks; no explicit completed replacement or future substitution commitment. Uses mask, finds cleaning easy and fit almost perfect except cheeks/nose; motivates use of other hydrating/moisturizing products credited with barrier repair, so mask-alone efficacy is unestablished. One Experiment acquisition category; no gift, repurchase, stockpile or return. Metadata separately identifies Acid Lime/SMALL, verified buyer and unrewarded; formula/version unknown.

eratch; Reddit 1i30kik, 2025-01-16; score 12, material_positive=false/not_interpreted, observation time unavailable; independence posture unavailable. Thread title resolves brand to Regimen Lab. Reports acquiring cream 2.0 seeking a healing moisturizer after excessive tret use and also picking up cleanser. Favorable cream experience supports intention to try more; cleanser is nice but small, with greater interest in serums/moisturizers. Science/formulation praise is personal assessment. These are other-brand acquisitions and prospective interest, not Experiment buying, proven healing, repurchase or completed routine replacement. Context post supplies brand reference only; its author, date and engagement are unavailable.
